Notes: Drink water before you do anything else — the cabin has dried everyone out and it is about to get humid.

Activity: Immigration, bags, and EasyCards for eleven
Notes: Buy the EasyCards at the MRT counter in the arrivals hall while everyone's still together — it's a much smoother job as one group than chasing it later in ones and twos. The littlest one can usually ride free on a lap under the standard height threshold, so eleven cards covers the family. Then go find the pre-booked van.
A short detour off the highway for a proper breakfast before the family visit — luggage stays snug in the van the whole time.

"拿靠" is Linkou's own old nickname, and this local chain — the Zhongxiao branch, 忠孝一路9號, about five minutes from Minzu Road — is where the town actually eats, not a stop built for tourists. The crispy egg crepe is the one to order; radish cake with a fried egg is the heartier backup for anyone who wants more than a crepe. Casual counter-and-table seating. Call ahead for a table of twelve (≈02-2600-8995) — see the reviews below for why that matters. If it can't fit the whole family, Linkou Market's grab-and-go stalls (政宗包子, 蒸宴小籠包) are two minutes from Minzu Road and open before 5am.
Five easy minutes further into the old town, where the family is already waiting.

Activity: No. 83 Minzu Road — the family visit
Notes: The van waits outside, so there's no clock to watch — let the visit run long if it wants to. Take a group photo here; it's the one stop on this trip that belongs entirely to your family.
The last leg of the morning — hotel next. Don't be surprised if half the van is asleep within ten minutes.
Far too early for the rooms to be ready — hand everything to the bell desk and head straight back out. A proper lunch is waiting somewhere in Zhongshan.

No fixed plan — today the whole rest of the afternoon is wide open. The Zhongshan MRT area and Shuangcheng Street are packed with boutiques, bookshops and cafés, a short walk or one stop away — split up, shop, grab lunch as you go, sneak a nap back at the hotel, or just find somewhere cool to sit. Regroup by 18:15 for the night market.
Three taxis for the twelve of us, four to a car. Ten to fifteen minutes from Zhongzheng.
One short street, food and nothing but food — no trinket stalls to wade through. It's the kindest night market in Taipei for tired legs, and the best one for old-school Taiwanese cooking.
An early night tonight. Tomorrow's tea hills are gentle going, but an early start still pays off at the gondola queue.
A slower start today, on purpose — let everyone's body clock catch up before the day begins.
Take the Brown Line all the way to the end of the line. The gondola entrance is a well-signposted three-minute walk from Exit 2.

Buy the NT$300 day pass for unlimited rides, so you can hop off at Zhinan Temple for free on the way down. If the kids fancy a glass floor underfoot, add NT$50 for a Crystal Cabin — just note its queue runs separately, and longer.

Activity: The Camphor Trail and the tea slopes
Notes: A flat, paved loop through working tea terraces, with Taipei 101 rising out of the basin behind you the whole way. Benches and shade line the path, and the Tea Promotion Centre along the route pours free tastings.

Address: Maokong tea houses near the terminal
Notes: Mountain Tea House (4.5) serves proper set meals for six with tea-leaf cooked dishes and a 101 view; Maokong Tea House (4.8) keeps it lighter — tieguanyin ice cream, boba, snacks. Book ahead, since Sunday lunch fills fast.

Activity: Sit with a pot of oolong, then drift down
Address: Maokong tea houses near the terminal
Notes: No one should be rushed out of a Maokong tea house. Linger over the pot, and when you're ready, ride down — hopping off at Zhinan Temple on the way if anyone's curious.
Non-negotiable in this heat, especially for the grandparents — shower, air-con, and horizontal for a while.

Address: Raohe St, Songshan — MRT Songshan exit 5
Notes: MRT to Songshan station, exit 5, and the market gate is right there. Start with the pepper buns near the temple end — the queue looks daunting but moves in about eight minutes.
Tomorrow the mid-bus at 08:30 for Yilan. A normal bedtime tonight is enough — a towel for wet feet at Qingshui.

A sit-down breakfast — the bus comes to the door. The tunnel is a highway, not a mountain road, but tablets still help anyone who hates enclosed space. A small towel for wet feet at Qingshui; no swimsuit unless someone wants the optional wooden bathhouse.

Activity: Mid-bus: hotel → Zhuangwei, through the tunnel
Notes: Same 中巴 type as Day 1 — a 19–20 seater, waiting all day, not Kamalan coaches plus taxis. Weekday morning through the Xueshan Tunnel is about seventy to ninety minutes to Zhuangwei. Tell the driver 蘭陽動植物王國，壯圍鄉紅葉路62-13號. Arrive at opening: weekdays start at 10:00, not 09:30.
Maps Link: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=蘭陽動植物王國+宜蘭縣壯圍鄉紅葉路62-13號

Activity: Lanyang Flora & Fauna Kingdom — kangaroos, capybara, teddy sheep
Notes: Walk-up tickets: adult about NT$280, ages 12 and under / 65+ about NT$180, under 90 cm or under two free. Feed is extra. Two hours: 10:00 flying-squirrel slot, goat race at 10:30, teddy-sheep feeding at 11:00, then kangaroos and capybara outdoors. Skip the plant DIY. Phone 0958-507-905.
Maps Link: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=蘭陽動植物王國+宜蘭縣壯圍鄉紅葉路62-13號

Activity: Short hop to lunch in Zhuangwei
Notes: About fifteen minutes southwest to Xinnan Road
Maps Link: on the way toward Yilan City. Seafood instead is Hai Zhi Wei on Zhongyang Road
column11: about ten minutes from the park.
column12: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=大嵌城甕缸雞+壯圍鄉新南路102-6號

Activity: Lunch — jar chicken and stir-fries, or seafood
Notes: Walk in at 大嵌城甕缸雞 — 03-938-7700 — open 11:00–20:00. Order à la carte: two jar-roast chickens (about NT$700 each; phone them at 11:00 from the park so the kiln is ready), clams, greens, tofu, rice. Cash. Ask for the bill around 13:10 so you are on the road by 13:20. Seafood instead: 壯圍海之味, 03-938-8616, No. 288 Sec. 2 Zhongyang, lunch until ~14:00, closed Wednesday.
Maps Link: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=大嵌城甕缸雞+壯圍鄉新南路102-6號

Notes: Forty to fifty minutes west across the Lanyang Plain. Tell the driver 清水地熱公園，三星路八段501巷150號. The last stretch is a narrow valley road — a 中巴 sometimes cannot enter. If it cannot, wait at 長埤湖停車場 and walk or shuttle the last ten minutes. Monday in September is the kinder version of this problem.
Maps Link: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=清水地熱公園+宜蘭縣大同鄉三星路八段501巷150號

Activity: Qingshui Geothermal Park — cook in the wells, soak your feet
Address: No. 150, Ln. 501, Sec. 8, Sanxing Rd, Datong, Yilan
Notes: Free entry. Buy eggs, corn and a bamboo basket at the visitor centre — spend about NT$60 per basket and the hire is free (NT$200 deposit, returned). Eggs eight to ten minutes, corn about twenty. Put the baskets in a numbered well, then sit in the free foot pools (about 40°C) while they cook. The wells themselves are 95°C — keep the 3-year-old on the path, not at the rim. This is not a swimsuit spa; 清水泉湯屋 is an optional extra if anyone still wants a body soak. Park closes at 17:00. Leave at 16:00 so the tunnel is still civilised.
Maps Link: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=清水地熱公園+宜蘭縣大同鄉三星路八段501巷150號

Notes: Further inland than the tunnel mouth, so the ride home is about ninety minutes on a Monday. Leave at 16:00, not 16:45. Wet feet and a highway is fine; a 17:00 closing plus the evening clog is not.
Home at a civilised hour, on purpose. Nearest food, lights out by 22:00 — lanterns tomorrow, bus at 10:00.

Activity: Breakfast — hotel, or Fu Hang Soy Milk
Notes: Fu Hang sits upstairs in the Huashan Market building by Shandao Temple, just minutes from the Airbnb — savoury soy milk, thick shaobing still warm from the griddle, youtiao fried to order. The queue is the stuff of legend: arrive at 08:00 or skip it entirely. The bus isn't until 10:00. Closed Mondays, so today you're in luck.

Tell the driver 十分瀑布, the park gate, not the station. Door to door is often 50–65 minutes after the morning rush; we keep seventy-five so a mid-bus on mountain roads still lands you before lunch. The 25-minute walk from the station is the bit you just bought out of the day.
Dropped at the gate. Entry is free and the viewing decks are level throughout. Carry water — September heat still finds you on a boardwalk.

Activity: Short hop to Shifen Old Street
Notes: Five to ten minutes. The driver can wait on the street or at the car park while you eat and linger.

Liou Gou's deboned chicken wing, stuffed with fried rice and grilled to a crackle, is the dish everyone comes here for. Afterwards, browse the stalls, watch a train rumble straight down the middle of the street, and pick out your lantern colours for later.

Activity: Deliberate slow block — tea, shade, sitting
Notes: This gap isn't filler — it's how the lantern still goes up at golden hour on a ten-hour clock. Air-conditioned cafés line the street. The optional hop to Jingtong is off the plan — leaving Jiufen at 18:45 will not wait for a side trip.

Write your wishes across all four sides with the brush, stand together on the tracks, and let go as one around 16:00–17:00 while the light turns gold. Roughly NT$200 a lantern, shared between two or three — and worth having one grown-up keep a hand on the three-year-old, well clear of the flame, while it lifts. This is the moment the whole trip has been building to.

Activity: Golden Waterfall — two minutes from the road
Notes: The stop the train plan dropped. Photograph from the roadside, do not wade. Then on to Jiufen while the light is still going gold.
Tell the driver 九份老街. About fifteen to twenty minutes. He can wait at the coach park while you climb.

You arrive just as the red lanterns are being lit. Steep steps everywhere. Settle the grandparents at a view teahouse and let everyone else climb. Be back at the coach park by 18:45 — the bus contract ends at 20:00.
Jiufen Teahouse (4.8) does interactive brewing while the mountainside drops away to the sea below. Sit down by 17:45 and leave the table by 18:35 so you are on the bus at 18:45.
About seventy-five minutes on a weekday evening. Leave Jiufen at 18:45, not later. If the driver says traffic looks heavy, leave at 18:30. The contract ends at 20:00.
Tired legs, full hearts, and a phone full of photos of a lantern drifting up into the dark. Home before the bus turns into a pumpkin.

Activity: Breakfast, and pack the day bag
Notes: Umbrella, water, and motion sickness tablets — the road up to Fuxing winds through a long series of bends. The bus comes to the hotel at 08:00.
Tell the driver 小烏來天空步道，桃園市復興區 — not 乌来 in New Taipei. About ninety minutes, freeway then the mountain road. Tablets before you board.

The glass platform cantilevers out over the falls. Anyone uneasy with heights can take the side path and still get the full waterfall view from solid ground. There's a suspension bridge on the far side for the brave. The skywalk normally needs an online slot booked in advance — see the note below.

Activity: Mid-bus down to Daxi Old Street
Notes: Same bus, same driver. Ask to be dropped on Heping Old Street, right where lunch is waiting.

Activity: Lunch — Hakka food on Daxi Old Street
Notes: This is Hakka country, and the local restaurants cook accordingly — salty, savoury, a little fatty, and exactly right after a morning outdoors.

Activity: The rest of the afternoon in Daxi Old Street
Notes: With the whole afternoon open, there's no reason to rush — and no need to sit down for another full meal after lunch. Walk Heping Road for the best-preserved baroque facades, duck into a woodwork shop or two, and graze a few of the stalls below instead of ordering big. Anyone who's had enough can settle into the arcades with a cold drink while the rest keep browsing.
About seventy-five minutes. Home in time for a quiet dinner; the farewell hotpot waits until Thursday.
Not the farewell hotpot — that is Thursday, after Hsu's. Tonight is whatever is nearest: Huashan, a convenience store, a noodle shop. Lights out by 22:00; Hsu's tomorrow.
Thursday is Hsu's and hotpot. Pack a change of shirt for the workshop.
Eat here. The noodles at 09:30 are lunch, and the mountain road is not the moment for an empty stomach. Motion-sickness tablets before you board.

A winding New Taipei mountain road, about an hour from Zhongzheng. This has to be a 中巴, not a nine-seat van — twelve of you still cannot legally fit in one. The driver waits through the session and then drops you in Ximending. Do not take bus 666; it will eat the morning.

Activity: Hsu's handmade noodles — DIY + flowing noodles
Address: No. 3, Sifenzi, Wutu Village, Shiding, New Taipei
Notes: Book the 09:30 session — handmade-noodle DIY plus 流水麵, about NT$550. You throw the dough, they walk you through the thirteen steps, then noodles come down a bamboo trough of cold mountain spring water and you catch them with chopsticks. That is lunch. Ages 6 and under are free; the 3-year-old watches the throwing and joins the catching. Closed Tuesdays; Monday is the Yilan day — so this sits on Thursday.

Activity: Van drops the group in Ximending
Notes: Not the hotel. Tell the driver 西門町 / 西門紅樓. Anyone who is actually full can skip the next snack stop; everyone else is two minutes from Ay-Chung.

Activity: Extra bites if anyone is still hungry
Notes: Ay-Chung mee sua and Lao Tian Lu braised meats are the two names worth knowing. Standing food, fast queues, no table of twelve required. Skip this entirely if Hsu's filled you up.

Activity: Red House and the pedestrian streets
Notes: This is the shopping stretch, not a forty-minute pose. The Red House's octagonal hall is full of small designer shops; the streets around it are streetwear, cinemas, and whatever the aunts point at. The outdoor craft market typically runs Thursday to Sunday — today is Thursday, so it should be on.

Activity: Longshan and Bopiliao — only if you still want a temple
Notes: Three MRT stops south on the blue line. A working temple, then the old street next door and Herb Lane for a cooling tea. Anyone who would rather keep shopping in Ximen just stays — the group does not have to move as one.

Activity: Back toward the hotel, then Zhongshan
Notes: MRT from Ximen. Anyone who wants Longshan peels off at 15:00; the rest can keep shopping until 16:30. The farewell table is at 18:30 — do not still be in Ximen at 18:00.
Wulao Hotpot in Zhongshan is polished and set up for groups; Lujiba Chengdu skewer hotpot (4.9) is the spicier, livelier option. Book for twelve.

Activity: Back to the hotel — pack properly tonight
Notes: Tomorrow morning is Dihua, then the 20:00 flight. Bags closed before you leave.
Round up everyone's purchases now — six days of night-market hauls add up fast, and someone's suitcase will not close without a fight.
Clear every room and hand it all to the bell desk. Carry only what the morning needs — you'll swing back for the bags at 14:30.
Two taxis over to Dadaocheng — ask the driver for the Yongle Market end and stroll north from there.

Activity: Dihua Street — gifts and old Taipei
Notes: Dried goods, tea, nougat, pineapple cakes, and bolts of fabric at Yongle Market — flat underfoot the whole way, arcaded against sun and rain, with cafés whenever the group needs to sit a while.

Rated 4.3. Refined Taiwanese cooking in a beautifully restored shophouse — the rice is the star here, alongside braised duck and shrimp rolls. Reserve for twelve. Yongle Market's stalls make a good casual fallback.
Count the bags, then count the people. Passports out and double-checked before anyone moves.
The same 20-seat 中巴 as Day 1, booked as a point-to-point send-off — not an hourly day. About fifty minutes door to door. A van will not fit twelve people and a week of luggage.

Four hours ahead of an international departure — deliberately generous, clearing the usual three-hour guideline with room to spare for an older group, a three-year-old's pace, and no shortage of bags.
Check the bags first, then eat. If anyone forgot a gift for someone back home, the airside pineapple cakes are the perfect way to spend the last of the cash.
Safe travels home, and welcome back with suitcases considerably fuller than they left.
